items.hint: Asking for $f^{-1}(9)$ is asking which input to $f$ produces the output $9$.
worked: $f^{-1}(9)$ is the input whose output is $9$, so set $2x+1=9$.
Undo the operations in reverse order: subtract $1$ to get $2x=8$.

items.hint: Write $y=3x-12$, swap $x$ and $y$, then undo the operations in the reverse of the order $f$ applied them.

items.stem: Let $f$ be a one-to-one function with inverse $f^{-1}$. Which statement is true for every such $f$?
items.hint: Test each claim against the one job an inverse has: send an output of $f$ back to the input it came from.
worked: The inverse undoes $f$, so feeding $f(x)$ into $f^{-1}$ must return the original $x$.
That is the definition: $f^{-1}(f(x))=x$ for every $x$ in the domain of $f$.
Test the others on $f(x)=2x$, where $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}$: that is not $\dfrac{1}{2x}$, and the product $f(x)\cdot f^{-1}(x)=x^{2}$ is not $x$.

Test the domain claim on $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$: $f$ has domain $x \ge 0$ and $f^{-1}(x)=x^{2}$ has domain $x \ge 0$ only because the range of $f$ is $y \ge 0$, so the matching set is the range, not the domain.

options.text: $f^{-1}(f(x))=x$ for every $x$ in the domain of $f$.
The domain of $f^{-1}$ is always the same as the domain of $f$.

items.stem: A student is asked for the inverse of $f(x)=x^{2}-9$ with domain $x \ge 0$. She writes $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x}+3$. Which choice repairs her work?
items.hint: Undo the two operations in reverse order: add $9$ first, and only then take the square root of that whole quantity.
worked: The domain $x \ge 0$ means the outputs of $f^{-1}$ must be nonnegative, so keep only the positive root: $y=\sqrt{x+9}$.
Her move $\sqrt{x+9}=\sqrt{x}+3$ is not legal; at $x=16$ it claims $\sqrt{25}=4+3$, so $5=7$.

items.stem: The function $f(x)=\sqrt{x-4}-1$ has domain $x \ge 4$. Which choice gives $f^{-1}$ together with its correct domain?
items.hint: The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$, so ask how small $\sqrt{x-4}-1$ can possibly get.
worked: Since $\sqrt{x-4} \ge 0$, the smallest output of $f$ is $-1$, so the range of $f$ is $y \ge -1$.
That range is the domain of the inverse: $f^{-1}(x)=(x+1)^{2}+4$ for $x \ge -1$.
